items.title: Musk explains why Tesla Robotaxi is not running at night, and lidar is the answer
items.topic: Musk explains why Tesla Robotaxi is not running at night, and lidar is the answer
items.summary: Elon Musk explained that Tesla's Robotaxi service is not operating at night due to the lack of lidar sensors, which are essential for safe navigation in low-light conditions. This highlights the ongoing debate over the necessity of lidar in autonomous vehicle systems and the challenges Tesla faces in achieving full autonomy.

items.title: EU vote on Tesla's supervised self-driving system pushed back
items.topic: EU vote on Tesla's supervised self-driving system pushed back
items.summary: The European Union has postponed its vote on Tesla's supervised self-driving system, delaying the regulatory decision that could impact the deployment of Tesla's autonomous technology in Europe. This delay reflects the cautious approach regulators are taking with advanced driver assistance systems.

items.title: Google rolls out new Gemini AI model but restricts access over safety concerns
items.topic: Google rolls out new Gemini AI model but restricts access over safety concerns
items.summary: Google has rolled out its new Gemini AI model but restricted access due to safety concerns, highlighting the company's cautious approach to deploying advanced AI technologies. The model's capabilities and potential applications in various fields, including autonomous vehicles, remain under scrutiny.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI sound the alarm on AI safety — and seek to shape how it’s controlled
items.topic: Anthropic and OpenAI sound the alarm on AI safety — and seek to shape how it’s controlled
items.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI have issued warnings about AI safety and are advocating for stricter controls on AI development. Their efforts to shape regulatory frameworks highlight the industry's growing awareness of the potential risks associated with advanced AI systems, including those used in autonomous vehicles.

items.title: Introducing NV-Reason-CT Open 3D CT VLM for Radiologist Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.topic: Introducing NV-Reason-CT Open 3D CT VLM for Radiologist Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.summary: NVIDIA has introduced NV-Reason-CT, an open 3D CT Vision-Language Model (VLM) designed for radiologist chain-of-thought reasoning. While primarily aimed at medical imaging, the model's advanced reasoning capabilities could have implications for perception and explainability in autonomous driving systems.

items.title: Mazda adds LiDAR to CX-6e, rolls out "self driving" tech in China
items.topic: Mazda adds LiDAR to CX-6e, rolls out "self driving" tech in China
items.summary: Mazda has added LiDAR to its CX-6e model and is rolling out self-driving technology in China, expanding its autonomous vehicle capabilities. This move underscores the growing importance of LiDAR in achieving higher levels of autonomy and the strategic focus on emerging markets for AV deployment.

items.title: Vision-Language-Action Autonomous Driving Agent with Language-based Memory
items.topic: Vision-Language-Action Autonomous Driving Agent with Language-based Memory
items.summary: The AD-Memo, proposed by researchers in a 2026 arXiv paper, addresses the limitations of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in memory-dependent tasks by introducing a language-based memory system. This system extends the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) mechanism to enhance interpretability and long-horizon driving scene understanding, making it a significant advancement in explainable AI for autonomous driving.

items.title: Localized Conformal Safety Monitoring with Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
items.topic: Localized Conformal Safety Monitoring with Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Researchers from a 2026 arXiv paper introduced Split Label-Localized Conformal Prediction (SLLCP), a post-hoc calibration layer for vision-language models (VLMs) in autonomous driving. SLLCP transforms unreliable VLM predictions into probabilistically calibrated safety assessments, improving the reliability and safety of trajectory monitoring in autonomous vehicles.

items.title: Learning to Explain While Planning: Rule-Aligned Diffusion Planning for Autonomous Driving
items.topic: Learning to Explain While Planning: Rule-Aligned Diffusion Planning for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: A 2026 arXiv paper proposes Rule-Aligned Diffusion Planning, a method that integrates driving rules into the trajectory generation process of diffusion planners. This approach enhances the safety and compliance of autonomous driving by providing rule-level explanations for trajectory adjustments, facilitating better failure diagnosis and targeted improvements.
